title: SBI Funds Management Shares List on Stock Exchanges in India's Largest Asset Manager IPO
excerpt: India's biggest mutual fund house, managing ₹12.5 lakh crore in assets, makes its stock market debut after a ₹9,813 crore offer-for-sale that drew 40 times oversubscription.
body:
• SBI Funds Management, India's largest mutual fund house with ₹12.5 lakh crore ($131 billion) in assets under management, listed on the NSE and BSE on July 21.
  • The ₹9,813 crore ($1.03 billion) IPO was entirely an offer-for-sale by parent State Bank of India and joint venture partner Amundi, with no fresh capital raised by the company.
  • The issue was oversubscribed roughly 40 times on its final day, with qualified institutional buyers leading demand.
  • Grey market premiums ahead of listing suggested a debut at 16-19% above the issue price of ₹574 per share, valuing the company at approximately ₹1.17 lakh crore ($12.2 billion).

SBI Funds Management, the country's largest asset management company by assets under management, began trading on the National Stock Exchange and BSE on Monday following a blockbuster initial public offering that ranks among the biggest Indian share sales of 2026. The listing caps a three-day subscription window that closed on July 16 with approximately 40 times oversubscription.

The IPO, priced at ₹545-574 per share, was structured entirely as an offer-for-sale. State Bank of India sold up to 12.83 crore shares while Amundi India Holding divested up to 7.54 crore shares, together offloading about 10 percent of the fund house's paid-up equity. SBI Funds Management itself does not receive any proceeds from the offering.

India's Mutual Fund Giant

SBI Funds Management is a joint venture between SBI, India's largest lender, and Amundi, Europe's biggest asset manager. The company oversees ₹12.5 lakh crore ($131.4 billion) in assets as of March 2026, a position that reflects both SBI's vast distribution network — spanning over 22,000 bank branches — and India's rapidly growing mutual fund industry.

"Ahead of the public issue, SBI Funds Management raised ₹1,655 crore through a pre-IPO placement, selling 2.88 crore shares to 30 institutional investors at ₹574 per share."

At the upper end of the price band, the company sought a valuation of approximately ₹1.17 lakh crore ($12.24 billion), positioning it between listed peers HDFC Asset Management Company (market cap ~$12.5 billion) and ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company (~$17.2 billion).

Brokerages assigned the company a price-to-earnings ratio of about 38 times at the issue price, which analysts at Geojit Financial Services described as "moderately lower" than listed peers. Swastika Investmart rated the issue a "Subscribe," citing the company's market leadership and healthy profitability.

Institutional Demand Dominated

Qualified institutional buyers drove the oversubscription, reflecting strong confidence among domestic and global fund managers. Ahead of the public issue, SBI Funds Management raised ₹1,655 crore through a pre-IPO placement, selling 2.88 crore shares to 30 institutional investors at ₹574 per share. Sovereign wealth funds including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Singapore's GIC were among those who expressed interest, according to Reuters.

The grey market premium in the days before listing hovered between ₹91 and ₹110 per share, implying a debut at roughly 16 to 19 percent above the issue price.

What It Signals for Indian Markets

The listing is expected to set the stage for a busy second half of 2026 in India's primary market. Share sales from Reliance Jio and the National Stock Exchange of India are anticipated later this year, according to Reuters, and a strong SBI Funds Management debut would reinforce appetite for large-cap Indian offerings.

India's mutual fund industry has been on a sustained growth trajectory, with assets under management across the industry crossing ₹65 lakh crore as of June 2026. Monthly systematic investment plan (SIP) inflows have consistently exceeded ₹25,000 crore, reflecting a structural shift toward equity savings among Indian households.

For non-resident Indian investors, the listing provides a direct way to invest in the growth of India's fund management industry. With SBI's unmatched branch network providing steady distribution and Amundi's global expertise supporting product development, the company occupies a unique position in India's financial landscape.
